name: Familial Aortic Dissection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Familial Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of first-degree relative with documented thoracic aortic dissection or aneurysm
Confirmed thoracic aortic dissection by imaging or surgical findings
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with familial aortic disease (e.g., ACTA2, TGFBR1/2, MYH11)
Presence of thoracic aortic aneurysm ≥4.0 cm in diameter
Lack of clinical features suggestive of syndromic connective tissue disorders (e.g., Marfan syndrome, Loeys-Dietz syndrome)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis requires documented thoracic aortic dissection or aneurysm in the patient plus a first-degree relative with confirmed thoracic aortic disease.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory if family history and clinical findings are definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cystic medial necrosis of the aorta

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers unless secondary complications
imaging: CT angiography showing intimal flap and false lumen
Transesophageal echocardiography demonstrating aortic root involvement
MRI angiography for detailed vessel wall assessment
other: Family history of thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection
Histopathology showing cystic medial necrosis in aortic wall

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic connective tissue manifestations (e.g., lens dislocation, skeletal abnormalities)
Arterial tortuosity and aneurysms throughout vascular tree
Hypertelorism and bifid uvula or cleft palate
Mutations in TGFBR1 or TGFBR2 with syndromic features

redFlags: Sudden severe chest or back pain with tearing quality
Asymmetric blood pressure or pulse in limbs
references: Isselbacher EM. Thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysms. Circulation. 2005;111(6):816-828.
Loeys BL, et al. The revised Ghent nosology for the Marfan syndrome. J Med Genet. 2010;47(7):476-485.
MacCarrick G, et al. Loeys-Dietz syndrome: a primer for diagnosis and management. Genet Med. 2014;16(8):576-587.
